terms.comment: In the Roman Breviary Matins is the night office before Lauds; in the Byzantine rite the morning service is Orthros (Ὄρθρος), which English calls Matins. Both take their name from the morning: classical mātūtīnus, of the morning (Lewis & Short), as in Prudentius’s Hymnus mātūtīnus (Cath. 2).

sources: Prudentius’s title from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-prudentius).
